ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A double pulley is free to rotate about its axis through its center. The radii of the two pulleys are $R$ and $2R$. Two cords are wrapped in opposite directions on the pulleys and are attached to masses. As a result, the two tension forces acting on the pulley are equal and acting downwards as shown in the image below so that $F_1 = 2F_2$. When released from rest, what will be the direction of the angular acceleration?

Reasoning: Take the counterclockwise direction as positive. The downward force F1 at the left small radius R produces a counterclockwise torque about the center, with magnitude F1R; the downward force F2 at the right large radius 2R produces a clockwise torque about the center, with magnitude F2(2R). From Στ = Iα, it can be known that the angular acceleration α = 0.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing F1 acting downward on the left side of the smaller pulley of radius R, and F2 acting downward on the right side of the larger pulley of radius 2R. Assign a sign convention, e.g. counterclockwise positive. The left downward force produces a torque +F1 R, while the right downward force produces a torque -F2(2R), because the cords are wrapped on opposite sides/directions. From the text, F1 = 2F2, so the torque magnitudes are F1 R = 2F2 R and F2(2R) = 2F2 R. The net torque is zero, so using Στ = Iα, the angular acceleration is zero; there is no direction of angular acceleration.

method.method_draft: Use a virtual-displacement/work argument. From the image, the two cords are wrapped in opposite directions: a small rotation of the pulley would let one cord move by arc length Rθ on the inner pulley and the other by arc length 2Rθ on the outer pulley, with opposite rotational effects. The generalized rotational work from the tensions for a small angular displacement θ is proportional to F1(Rθ) - F2(2Rθ), with the sign difference coming from the opposite wrapping shown. Substituting the text relation F1 = 2F2 gives F1Rθ = 2F2Rθ and F2(2R)θ = 2F2Rθ, so the virtual works cancel. Therefore the generalized torque is zero, and released from rest the pulley has no angular acceleration.
